content.title: When is Artemis 2 rocket launch in Florida? Tourist guide, hotel info
content.text: Updated March 25, 2026, 12:11 p.m. ETYou're guaranteed to get a beautiful view of the rocket launch anywhere on Florida's Space Coast (so long as weather and cloud cover cooperate).Brevard County, Florida, home to NASA's Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, is a long county with 72 miles of coast.Watching a rocket launch at the beach is popular for tourists and locals. See @florida_today on Instagram!The closer you are to NASA and Cape Canaveral, the better the view you'll have of the SLS rocket launch, pending weather and clouds.It's spring break and fabulous weather − what can make a trip to Florida better?How about a mega moon rocket launch?As NASA preps for its Space Launch System rocket launch, the Space Coast could see a bump in visitors. NASA's milestone Artemis II launch to the moon from Kennedy Space Center may draw 400,000 visitors to Florida's Space Coast − and hotels here are filling up.If you're a tourist or space fan interested in watching the historic Artemis rocket launch in Florida, you may be wondering, where should I stay to watch NASA's Artemis 2 rocket liftoff? How far are Orlando theme parks to Kennedy Space Center? What cities should I look for if I want to book lodging?Travel sites online show there are hotel rooms and vacation rentals available the weekend of March 27 to April 3 − though they are expected to fill up fast. NASA has other launch attempts if the SLS doesn't launch the evening of Wednesday, April 1.NASA continues working toward a possible launch as early as 6:24 p.m. April 1, 2026 – near the tail end of Brevard County's bustling spring-break tourist season.The Artemis launch and spring break vacation contribute to the many sold-out queries. Because Space Coast hotels and vacation rentals are filling up, we compiled a guide with tips on where to stay and what to look up.What is NASA's Artemis 2 mission?NASA's giant moon rocket is back on the launch pad at Kennedy Space Center in Florida, setting the stage for what appears to be an imminent launch of the Artemis 2 lunar mission.The rocket – topped with the Orion crew capsule – is vertical and visible along Florida's Atlantic coast. And now that the three Americans and one Canadian who will hitch a ride to Earth's orbit are isolating to avoid sickness before the mission, the stage is set for an imminent launch of what will be the first U.S. human lunar mission in five decades.As early as April, NASA will send the four astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon in a crucial venture that will set the stage for a moon landing in as little as two years.When is the Artemis 2 launch date? NASA targets April liftoff in FloridaNASA is working toward an April 1 launch of its historic Artemis 2 mission from the Kennedy Space Center in Florida.But if the weather or any other factors were to cause the launch to be delayed, several other days in April remain possibilities under NASA's timeline, including April 2-6 and April 30.So far, the currently announced available launch times are as follows:6:24 p.m. ET Wednesday, April 1, 20267:22 p.m. ET Thursday, April 2, 20268 p.m. ET Friday, April 3, 20268:53 p.m. ET Saturday, April 4, 20269:40 p.m. ET Sunday, April 5, 2026, Easter holiday10:36 p.m. ET Monday, April 6, 2026NASA said it has the opportunity to launch four out of those six days if needed.What is Artemis 2? Will there be a moon landing?Hitching a ride atop NASA's Space Launch System rocket, four Artemis 2 astronauts are due to pilot an Orion capsule on a 10-day trip around the moon. While no moon landing is in store for the mission, the crew will test systems and hardware for future expeditions to the surface while traveling up to 6,000 miles beyond the far side of the moon – the farthest humans have ever ventured in space.While NASA tested its spacecraft during the Artemis 1 mission in 2022, Artemis 2 will be the first time that the SLS rocket and the Orion capsule will fly with humans aboard.What does a Florida rocket launch from Kennedy Space Center or Cape Canaveral look like?Photos of NASA Artemis I rocket launch in 2022 from Kennedy Space Center in Florida NASA Artemis rocket launch: What Florida cities should I search for when booking online?You're guaranteed to get a beautiful view of the rocket launch anywhere on the Space Coast − so long as the weather and cloud cover cooperate, of course. But if you're not from the Brevard County area and you're just visiting, below is a list of the cities you should put in your search queries and the approximate miles away from Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.The Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex, which charges admission, provides a stunning view and is among the closest public access places to the launch pad (see below).'On the mainland.' What that means for watching a Florida rocket launchBrevard County in Florida, home to NASA's Kennedy Space Center and Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, is a long county with 72 miles of coast. Watching a rocket launch at the beach is popular for tourists and locals. If you're "on the mainland" here, that means you're blocks or miles from the beach. However, the Banana River and Indian River Lagoon run through Brevard, and almost all of these cities on this section below offer a riverfront view perfect for a launch. The closer you are to NASA and Cape Canaveral, the better the view you'll have of the SLS rocket launch, pending weather and cloud cover, of course!Mims, Florida, is about 20 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterTitusville, Florida, is about 15 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterPort St. John, Florida, is about 15 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterCocoa, Florida, is about 15 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterMerritt Island, Florida, is about 15 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterViera, Florida, is about 30 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterMelbourne, Florida, is about 35 to 45 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterWest Melbourne, Florida, is about 45 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterPalm Bay, Florida, is about 40 to 50 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterIf you're staying 'on the beach' and want to watch a Florida rocket launch, what cities to look up?Watching a rocket launch from the beach is so Space Coast. And so Florida.At NASA's Kennedy Space Center, Launch Pad 39A has a well-known history, as it was the pad that sent the Apollo 11 moon landing astronauts (Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins) on their historic journey. However, the launch pad has seen a pause in action due to SpaceX working to finalize the Starship tower and launch pad on the site.NASA's Artemis II crewed launch will be from Launch Pad 39B.These are the beach cities you should put in your search queries and the approximate mileage from Kennedy Space Center. As mentioned above, the closer you are to NASA and Cape Canaveral, the better the view you'll have of the SLS rocket launch, pending weather and cloud cover.Cape Canaveral, Florida, is about 15 miles away from NASA's Kennedy Space CenterCocoa Beach, Florida, is about 20 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterSatellite Beach, Florida, is about 30 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterIndian Harbour Beach, Florida, is about 30 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterIndialantic, Florida, is about 40 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterMelbourne Beach, Florida, is about 40 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterOther Florida cities to watch NASA Artemis rocket launch and drive time from Kennedy Space CenterIf you don’t mind a drive, the next few sections include a list of cities (and counties) outside of the Space Coast of Florida (Melbourne, Cocoa Beach, Cape Canaveral area) to put in your search queries for a place to stay. We’ll include the approximate mileage (and average traffic time estimates) from NASA's Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex.Here's a tip: Leave early to allow yourself plenty of time to navigate rush hour/spring break traffic, time to find parking and get situated.Volusia County is north of Kennedy Space Center. How far is Daytona International Speedway to Cape Canaveral, Florida?Oak Hill, Florida, is about 35 miles away from NASA's Kennedy Space Center, minimum 40 minutesPort Orange, Florida, is about 55 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum about an hourNew Smyrna Beach, Florida, is about 50 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum about an hourDaytona Beach, Florida, is about 65 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum about an hour and 10 minutesIndian River County is south of NASA. How far is Vero Beach to Cape Canaveral, Florida?Sebastian, Florida, is about 65 to 70 miles away from NASA's Kennedy Space Center, minimum about an hour and 15 minutesVero Beach, Florida, is about 70 to 80 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum about 75 to 90 minutesWabasso, Florida, is about 60 to 75 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum about 70 to 90 minutesSt. Lucie County is south of Kennedy Space Center. How far from Fort Pierce to Cape Canaveral, Florida?Fort Pierce, Florida, is about 90 to 95 miles away from NASA's Kennedy Space Center, minimum about 90 minutesJensen Beach, Florida, is about 100 to 110 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum 90 minutes to two hoursMartin County is south of NASA. How far from Stuart, Florida, to Kennedy Space Center?Stuart, Florida, is about 115 miles away from NASA's Kennedy Space Center, about two hoursHobe Sound, Florida, is about 130 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, about two hoursOrange County, west of Port Canaveral, home to Orlando theme parks. How far is Disney World to NASA's Kennedy Space Center?East Orlando, Florida, is about 45 to 60 miles away from NASA's Kennedy Space Center, minimum about an hourUniversity of Central Florida, is about 35 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum about 50 minutesWalt Disney World Resort in Orlando, Florida (specifically Magic Kingdom, Hollywood Studios, Animal Kingdom and Epcot theme parks), is about 55 to 70 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum about an hour to 90 minutesUniversal Orlando Resort in Florida (specifically Universal Studios, Islands of Adventure, Epic Universe and Volcano Bay parks), is about 55 to 65 miles away from Kennedy Space Center, minimum about an hour to 90 minutesWhile you're on the Space Coast in Florida, things to do, Florida attractionsWhile you're here to see NASA's Space Launch System mega moon rocket launch, might as well make it a mini-vacation.There are plenty of things to do and places to go. For example, the Space Coast has 72 miles of beach, and some of the best surfers in the world (we're looking at you, Kelly Slater), grew up in this area. Coincidentally, it's "spring break season" and picture-postcard weather in Florida.Aside from Kennedy Space Center, the Space Coast is home to Port Canaveral, the second busiest port in the world, and Brevard Zoo.Places to stay include vacation rentals, bed and breakfasts, condo rentals, campgrounds and hotels.Campgrounds in Brevard County and Central FloridaMaking the drive to Florida's Space Coast in a camper? Consider these options below from Brevard County Parks and Recreation:Manatee Hammock, a 26-acre campground in Titusville 8 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterWickham Park, a 391-acre campground in Melbourne 31 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterLong Point Park, an 84-acre campground in Melbourne Beach 52 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterFor a full list of Brevard County Parks and Recreation campgrounds, visit brevardfl.gov/ParksAndRecreation.There are, of course, some campgrounds just outside the Space Coast.Sebastian Inlet State Park in Melbourne Beach is 51 miles away from Kennedy Space Center. Visit floridastateparks.org/Sebastian-Inlet.Donald McDonald Park in Sebastian, is 71 miles away from Kennedy Space CenterFor a list of Indian River County Parks and Recreation campgrounds, visit ircgov.com/parksandrecreation.Watch some rocket launches with NASA+ on Prime VideoWatch NASA+ content with Amazon Prime VideoNASA content, including some rocket launches, is available to watch through NASA+ on desktop, both from its official site and YouTube. The platform is also available to download as a mobile app on smartphones.All NASA+ content is also available to those who have Prime Video downloaded on any of their devices – whether it be a smartphone or smart TV.The content, which does not require a Prime subscription to view, is one of Prime Video's FAST channels (free ad-supported television). Viewers can find it under Prime's Live TV section at the top of the screen when they open the app.Sangalang is a lead digital producer for USA TODAY Network.
